Q1 2025 revenue declined 7% to $329.3M - attributed to slowed Q1 velocity, timing/structure of the US distributor incentive program, and increased retail promotional programs, vs. a very strong Q1 2024 (ESSENTIALS launch, elevated promo takeovers).
Management framed the softness as temporary 'noise,' not structural; business fundamentals strengthened through the quarter with positive momentum into Q2.

Gross margin expanded 110 bps to 52.3% on sourcing efficiencies for raw and packaging materials; the ~50% full-year peg is a core-Celsius (pre-Alani) number; Q3/Q4 hedged on unknown tariffs/inflation.
Adjusted EBITDA margin compressed to 21.2% (from 24.7%) on Alani Nu transaction expenses and continued investment in global sales, marketing, and organizational infrastructure.

Alani Nu acquisition closed April 1, 2025 (a second $1B brand); reflected in Q2; funded with $900M debt, ~$400M cash, remainder stock; Q2 will carry inventory step-up purchase-accounting noise and higher D&A.
Celsius/Alani Nu cannibalization minimal - ~15% crossover per Circana; both portfolios over-index against other leading category brands.
Easier comps begin June 2025 - after the next 4-5 weeks of peak revenue hurdles, Celsius cycles much easier comps; back half of 2024 was softer.

No destocking - DSD-network depletions (COBOs and FOBOs) stable this quarter and at prior year-end; some non-DSD club timing/sequencing from Q4 into Q1; a Costco MVM event created prior-period pipe-fill.
Costco scanner data was up; reported softness from MVM pipe-fill timing and a revenue/ARR-as-%-of-sales working-capital nuance, not lost distribution.
Celsius took pricing in Q4 2024 (rolling through); flexible/opportunistic on additional pricing but cautious given consumers trading down from singles to multipacks and seeking promos.
Innovation a key growth driver - new core Vibe and ESSENTIALS flavors; summer innovation Playa Vibe, Retro Vibe, Mango Lemonade; CELSIUS HYDRATION launched into the $1.4B hydration powder category.

A public Alani Nu modeling call planned for late May / early June - pro forma combined-business reviews and purchase-accounting detail (inventory step-up, intangible/fixed-asset valuations, increased D&A).
A bold story-driven LIVE FIT summer marketing campaign begins this summer - first time the company has built a holistic campaign.
Eric Hanson appointed first President & COO in March (near-three-decade food/beverage exec with prior PepsiCo experience); Big Beverage facility fully integrated, room for a second production line.
Continued retail shelf-space gains expected in Q2 and Q3; analyst referenced an internal expectation of 15-20% shelf reset wins.
Energy category resilient on both dollars and volume; sugar-free surpassed full-sugar varieties for the first time in 2024; female consumers a large underserved segment, strengthened by Alani Nu.

Co-branded and/or dedicated coolers under evaluation depending on retailer footprint - co-branded coolers in the works for smaller-format stores; Alani Nu cross-channel opportunity (Amazon, foodservice, colleges, on-premise).
Alani Nu is ~18-24 months behind Celsius on the P&L profile (excluding step-up); standalone gross margin mid-40s / low-end mid-40s, working up to Celsius's profile.
Why is the energy category accelerating while most of CPG decelerates, and what is behind it?

Q1 was strong for energy, which has been resilient on dollars and volume over several years; attributed to health and wellness trends and a high volume of competitor innovation driving consumer excitement and trial.
What specifically is the company doing to increase velocity?

Q1 got off to a slow start; a more balanced approach this year after 2024's front-loaded innovation, distribution gains and promo; leaning into LIVE FIT-based programs and brand-DNA research to bring more consumers into the sugar-free segment.
Bridge the ~2% retail sales growth to the high-single-digit North America reported decline; parse underlying shipment/depletion trends after stripping the noise.

Slow start, increased competition, improving exit velocity; retailers leaned heavily on specific brands in 2024 launches vs. a balanced approach this year; cycling distributor incentives. Bridge: scanner ~-4% vs. -7% on books and records - a couple of points from promos/incentives, some non-DSD pipe-fill into Q4 2024. Primary-network depletions (COBOs, FOBOs) in good shape, little noise.
Broad view on category pricing (Monster priced ~75% of its portfolio; Red Bull uncertain) and the plan for pricing and promotion for the balance of the year.

Opportunistic opportunities to take additional pricing; confident in the brands but cautious given consumers trading down from singles to multipacks and seeking promos. Q4 2024 pricing rolling through gives flexibility on promotional activity amid consumer uncertainty.
More color on spring shelf-space expansion, dimensionalized for core Celsius and Alani Nu, and how to activate consumers around those gains versus last year.

Summer innovation (Playa Vibe, Retro Vibe, Mango Lemonade) expected to gain placements; secondary placements and checkout coolers major wins at large national retailers. Strong optimism on Alani Nu distribution gains - 2026 buyer/key-account meetings upcoming, summer momentum, $1B retail sales milestone, loyal female base.

Whether the steep Costco decline reflected lost distribution or destocking; North America sales down excluding the allowance change; help quantifying destocking vs. sell-out and the sequential phasing of allowances/destocking.

Reiterated the -4% scanner vs. -7% bridge (a couple of points promos/incentives). Costco scanner up; an MVM event created prior-period pipe-fill, plus a Costco-specific revenue/ARR-as-%-of-sales working-capital nuance, no underlying issue. Allowance phasing: ~2 pts pressure in Q1 and Q2, flipping to ~2 pts benefit in Q3 and Q4. No destocking - DSD depletions stable; only non-DSD club timing Q4 into Q1. Strong gross profit mitigated allowance pressure, flowed to EBITDA.
Color on the strong gross margin despite increased incentives/allowances, how sustainable it is, and watchouts from aluminum.

Great shape near-term - benefiting from scale, orbit model, organizational structure; aluminum 'knock-on-wood' not significantly impactful currently. Tariff outcomes unknown long-term, but Q2 still strong. ~50% gross margin pegged for the year; back half 'kind of an unknown' on inflation/tariffs; supply-chain structure set up as a sustainable long-term program.
Formats/retailers where Alani Nu outperforms core Celsius and how to cross-pollinate; branded cooler placements and the opportunity for co-branded coolers given limited cannibalization.

Great opportunities across all three brands (core Celsius, ESSENTIALS, Alani Nu) - Alani Nu in convenience, Amazon, restaurants/foodservice, colleges, on-premise. Cannibalization minimal at ~15% crossover (Circana); both portfolios over-index vs. leading brands. Energy merchandised together in energy sets; cooler placements a top KPI; evaluating co-branded and/or dedicated coolers, with co-branded coolers in the works for smaller-format stores.
Given the tailwinds (new innovation, 15-20% shelf reset wins, easier comps, new marketing campaign), conviction that core revenue trends improve from here.

Tailwinds favorable, especially after the next 4-5 weeks of peak revenue hurdles; from June, Celsius cycles much easier comps and is seeing improving velocity. Cited the category's return to strong growth, strong brand positioning, improving fundamentals, gross-profit improvements, the Big Beverage acquisition, orbit-model efficiencies, and the strength of operating a portfolio (wider pricing/promotional strategies).
How the international business is performing market-by-market relative to expectations.

Cautiously optimistic on international with a strict strategic new-market-entry approach; new-market expansion well received, better than initially expected; Australia/New Zealand launches with key retailers brought new consumers and share gains. International a growth area with additional markets in 2026, 2027 and beyond; 2025 focus on building Q4 2024-launched core markets.
Sequential Gross Margin & Alani Nu Layering
Any known headwinds causing sequential gross margin moderation from Q1, and considerations for how Alani Nu layers in from a gross-profit perspective.

The ~50% was the core Celsius business margin; a late-May / early-June modeling call will cover Alani Nu consolidation, including inventory step-up noise (a purchase-accounting issue). Comfortable with the core-business level; Q3/Q4 harder to call.
